deskyard cp: copy files to or from a desktop

Usage: deskyard [-d NAME] cp SRC DST

Copies a file or directory between this machine and a desktop; write the
desktop side as NAME:/path (NAME is a remote; an empty NAME, as in :/path,
means the chosen remote). A file lands at DST, or inside DST when it is an
existing directory. A directory's contents land in DST, which is created (like
`cp -r SRC/. DST`). SRC - reads stdin; DST - writes to stdout (a tar stream
for a directory). Files land as user; inside a desktop, two local paths are
copied locally.

Arguments:
  SRC        path        required  local path, -, or NAME:/path
  DST        path        required  local path, -, or NAME:/path

Prints: nothing, unless DST is - (the file's bytes or a tar stream)

Examples:
  deskyard cp ./report.pdf alice:/workspace/
  deskyard cp ./site alice:/workspace/site
  deskyard cp alice:/workspace/out.csv .

Where: on the chosen remote (-d NAME); inside a desktop without a remote it acts locally
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error
